RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer | Python
rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 21 years of experience in Python, Go and C++, building distributed services and fleet telematics software. Experience includes GPS data ingestion, high-volume APIs, PostgreSQL and cloud deployment on GCP. Currently focused on returning to hands-on individual contributor work; recent coding has centred on Python internal tooling and cost dashboard scripts.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages and frameworks: Python, FastAPI, Django, Flask, Tornado, asyncio, Go, C++
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS (EC2, S3; limited experience)
Observability and APIs: Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, gRPC, Protobuf
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, automated testing, technical hiring, people management

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH | 2019–Aug 2026
- Led the platform organisation of 45 engineers across five teams, responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
- Drove a strangler-fig migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python 3 and Go services on GKE. Playback API availability improved from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Set up a service template using FastAPI or Go, OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics and Terraform modules.
- Built an internal cost dashboard using BigQuery billing exports and Looker Studio. Rightsizing and committed-use discounts reduced cloud spend by 31%, or EUR 4.2M per year.
- Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
- Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and conducted more than 200 interviews.

Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH | 2015–2019
- Led technical development of the playback API using Python, Tornado, an internal framework, Cassandra and Redis.
- Designed and wrote most of a Go entitlement service determining playback eligibility by subscription, region and device. It handled 120,000 requests per second at peak with p99 latency under 15 ms.
- Used Cassandra and local in-memory caching for the entitlement service; its technology stack also included gRPC, Redis and Kubernetes.
- Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.

Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG | 2010–2015
- Built backend software for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
- Led a team of six developers on the route-history product.
- Co-invented a granted German patent for adaptive GPS sampling to reduce vehicle-fleet data volume, 2013.

Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH | 2005–2010
- Developed industrial data acquisition software in C++ and Python on Linux and embedded x86.
- Built a Python test harness used by QA for eight years.

OPEN-SOURCE EXPERIENCE
Maintainer, Python retry library | 2012–2018
- Maintained a small Python library using pytest and tox; the project gained approximately 1,500 GitHub stars. Handed over maintenance in 2018.

EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. in Computer Science, equivalent to MSc | Rhine Valley University | 2005

LANGUAGES
German and Italian: native | English: fluent

PUBLICATIONS AND TALKS
- “Running Python at 100k rps” — conference talk, 2018
- “Cost is a feature” — internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear section headings, consistent reverse-chronological experience, credible technical depth, and strong quantified outcomes. The 99.5% to 99.95% availability improvement, 120,000 requests/second entitlement service, 31% cloud-cost reduction, and 300,000-vehicle telematics platform provide excellent evidence of impact. The summary also appropriately explains the transition from engineering leadership back to hands-on individual-contributor work. The main content limitation is that the document remains somewhat leadership-heavy for a backend engineer role, while recent hands-on coding is described only generally. It is nevertheless honest about that limitation rather than overstating current implementation work.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong: the CV uses standard headings, plain text, conventional date formatting, searchable technology names, and no apparent tables, columns, graphics, headers, footers, or unusual formatting. Keyword coverage is particularly good for Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, cloud deployment, distributed systems, automated testing, and logistics/telematics. AI screening probability is high for the core backend, Python, cloud, event-processing, observability, and logistics criteria. Screening may be weaker for exact terms that the CV does not substantiate, especially REST APIs, Docker, CI/CD, schema migrations, and query tuning. These should not be added without truthful supporting evidence. One small ATS opportunity is that the CV mentions a Python test harness and pytest/tox in the document but does not place pytest or tox in the main Technical Skills section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns very well with the role's Python/backend, cloud deployment, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, event-ingestion, logistics, and technical-documentation themes. Fleet telematics and GPS ingestion are especially relevant to a shipment-tracking platform, and the on-call guidelines, RFC process, architecture reviews, and service-template work align with Tessel's ownership and reliability culture. English is explicitly listed as fluent and the technical talks support the ability to explain trade-offs clearly. The candidate's material does not establish Docker, REST API design/consumption, query tuning, live-data schema migrations, or CI/CD, so those are genuine requirement gaps rather than document defects. Dutch and French are also not present. AWS experience is listed but accurately qualified as limited, while the role uses AWS; this is a fit consideration, not a CV-writing defect.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, ATS-focused improvements:
1. In the Technical Skills section under “Other” or in a new “Testing” category, add “pytest, tox” because the CV already documents a Python test harness maintained with pytest and tox in the Open-Source Experience section. Example: “Testing: automated testing, pytest, tox”.
2. In the Director of Engineering, Platform entry, change “Set up a service template using FastAPI or Go” to “Set up a service template for FastAPI and Go services, including OpenTelemetry tracing, Prometheus metrics, and Terraform modules.” This uses clearer ATS-searchable phrasing while remaining supported by the candidate portfolio.
3. In the Professional Summary, make the individual-contributor positioning slightly more prominent by changing the final sentence to: “I am now returning to hands-on individual-contributor work; recent coding has centred on Python internal tooling and cloud-cost dashboard scripts.” This keeps the existing truthful disclosure while making the target role clearer to recruiters.
4. In the Principal Engineer entry, make the API and backend-service scope more explicit without adding unsupported REST terminology. For example, change “Led technical development of the playback API using Python, Tornado, an internal framework, Cassandra and Redis” to “Led technical development of a high-volume Python playback API and backend service using Tornado, an internal framework, Cassandra and Redis.”
5. In the Senior Software Engineer entry, change “Built backend software for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles” to “Built backend software for fleet telematics and GPS event ingestion from 300,000 vehicles.” This better matches the shipment-tracking job's event-ingestion terminology without claiming EDI or carrier-event experience.
6. Keep “AWS (EC2, S3; limited experience)” as written. Do not replace it with broader AWS, Docker, CI/CD, REST, schema-migration, or query-tuning claims because those capabilities are not established in the supplied candidate information.
